verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit documents incremental review of new changes as distinct from a full review, and its auto-review settings imply reviews continue as commits are added (they can pause after a set number of commits). The request-changes workflow syncs the review decision with resolved feedback, but the evidence never says the re-review tracks which earlier findings were fixed or avoids repeating old comments. Missing for 10: explicit docs that a push automatically triggers the incremental re-review, documented tracking of fixed versus outstanding comments, no-duplicate-comment behavior, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, pushing new commits triggers an incremental re-review that tracks what was fixed instead of repeating old comments
